title: iOS app, UI and enablement
summary: SwiftUI shell, rule editing, and the Settings-enablement screen
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Enablement APIs verified in iOS SDK 26.2 headers.

The SwiftUI app that owns the rules the two extensions consume. Serves R4, R7, R8 and the iOS half of R2 and R6.

ENABLEMENT (R4) — THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE SCREEN. Until the user turns the extension on in Settings, nothing is filtered and the app looks broken.
- CXCallDirectoryManager getEnabledStatusForExtensionWithIdentifier:completionHandler: returns Unknown / Disabled / Enabled.
- openSettingsWithCompletionHandler: (iOS 13.4+) deep-links there. Use it rather than describing a path in prose.
- Re-check at launch AND on foreground. Not a one-time onboarding step — users switch it off later and system updates reset it.
- Treat Unknown as not-enabled for display but distinguish it in diagnostics; it usually means the extension has never loaded.
- While disabled, show a blocking screen. Do not show a normal rule list implying the app is working.

RULE EDITING (R2): create and edit deny/allow rules of every type. For each rule show the expansion count and per-platform verdict from F002's explain() — e.g. "matches 11,000 numbers" or "too broad for iPhone calls". Never silently drop or narrow a rule. Surface equally specific conflicting rules for the user to resolve.

AFTER ANY CHANGE: trigger CXCallDirectoryManager reloadExtensionWithIdentifier: so the extension re-expands.

TWO HONEST LIMITATIONS TO DESIGN AROUND, both verified absent from the SDK:
- No call history and no blocked-call callback, so R6's one-tap block is impossible. Design the best available path: clipboard detection when the app opens, a share-sheet entry point if reachable from the Phone app, and fast manual entry. None recover one-tap; do not pretend otherwise.
- The app cannot report that it blocked anything. There is no activity log to show, which is the single most-requested thing in this category. Decide how the main screen earns its place without one.

LOCALIZATION (R7): UI strings plus place names with user-language then English then prefix-only fallback.

SHARING: rules and datasets written to the App Group the extensions read.
